q: What is AI training or evaluation work?
a: It is paid task work that helps improve AI systems: rating or comparing chatbot answers against guidelines, writing prompts and example answers, and labelling text, images, audio or map data. The platforms we cover describe these tasks on their official pages.

It depends on the platform and project. DataAnnotation's general track asks for a bachelor's degree or equivalent real-world experience. Outlier says some projects need no degree while others need one. Prolific lists no degree requirement for its studies.

We cannot tell you, and nobody honest can promise a figure. Some platforms publish rate ranges, for example DataAnnotation's FAQ says general projects start at $25-$50 per hour, and Prolific sets a minimum of £6 / $8 per hour per study. Work availability depends on projects and your quality, so no platform guarantees hours.

q: Do I have to pay to join an AI training platform?
a: No. Legitimate platforms do not charge you to join. The US FTC says honest employers will never ask you to pay to get a job, Appen Experts says it will never ask you to pay anything to join its projects, and DataAnnotation says it charges no signup fees.

q: Can I do this from outside the US?
a: Some platforms accept many countries and others do not. Prolific publishes a list of supported countries. TELUS Digital sets residency rules per listing. Outlier asks for an ID and phone from your country of residence. Always check eligibility on the official signup page.

The platforms we checked pay through methods such as PayPal, bank transfer, Airtm, Payoneer or Stripe, depending on the platform and your location. Each platform page on this site lists the methods it states.
Usually not. Outlier states that contributors are independent contractors. Treat the work as contract income and check your local tax rules.

q: Why did I not hear back after applying?
a: Platforms receive many applications. DataAnnotation says it cannot reply to every applicant and will contact you if you pass and have matching work. Prolific uses a waitlist and invites people when tasks match their profile.
